more.def: A large, strong tree with hard wood that grows acorns.
examples: A squirrel climbed the old oak.
The oak gave shade to the whole yard.
The table was made of oak.

easy.def: Made of oak, a hard wood.

examples: The oaken door was thick and heavy.
An oaken chest stood at the foot of the bed.
They sat at a big oaken table.

easy.def: A long pole with a flat end used to row a boat.

more.def: A long pole with a flat blade at one end that you use to row a boat through the water.
examples: We pulled on the oars and the little boat glided across the lake.
He dipped the oar into the water.

easy.def: A man who rows a boat.

more.def: A man who rows a boat.
examples: The oarsman pulled hard on the oars.
Each oarsman kept time with the drum.
The oarsman was tired after the race.

easy.def: A green place with water in the desert.

more.def: A green area in the desert where there is water and trees, or any calm, pleasant place.
examples: The travelers found an oasis with palm trees and a pool of water.
The garden was a quiet oasis in the busy city.

more.def: A grain that grows on a tall grass and is used for food, such as oatmeal.
examples: Oats are used to make oatmeal.
The farmer grows oat in the field.
The oath was to tell the truth.
The new member took an oath.

more.def: A serious promise, often made in front of others.
examples: The witness took an oath to tell the truth.
The scouts took an oath to be kind.
The new president took the oath of office.

easy.def: A hot breakfast food made from oats.

more.def: A cooked breakfast food made from crushed oats and hot water or milk.
examples: I ate warm oatmeal with raisins.
The oatmeal was thick and sweet.

easy.def: A grain used to make oatmeal and feed horses.

more.def: A kind of grain that is grown on farms and used for oatmeal, cookies and animal feed.
examples: I ate a bowl of hot oats with honey for breakfast.
The farmer fed oats to the horses.
Mom baked oatmeal cookies with rolled oats.
